metadata.title: Workflow Patterns
metadata.abstract_summary: Real workflow requirements recur as a checklist of 20+ distinct control-flow patterns - sequence, parallel split and synchronization, multi-choice, arbitrary cycles, and more - and the major commercial workflow/BPM products of the time supported very different, inconsistent subsets of them, meaning a workflow written for one system could not be assumed portable to another.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
sections.text: Real workflow requirements recur as a checklist of 20+ distinct control-flow patterns - sequence, parallel split and synchronization, multi-choice, arbitrary cycles, and more - and the major commercial workflow/BPM products of the time supported very different, inconsistent subsets of them, meaning a workflow written for one system could not be assumed portable to another.

claims.text: Real workflow requirements recur as a checklist of 20+ distinct control-flow patterns - sequence, parallel split and synchronization, multi-choice, arbitrary cycles, and more - and the major commercial workflow/BPM products of the time supported very different, inconsistent subsets of them, meaning a workflow written for one system could not be assumed portable to another.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: Pattern-mining from workflow literature and vendor documentation to derive the pattern catalogue, followed by a systematic evaluation of major commercial workflow management systems of the early 2000s against every pattern, checking which each product actually supports.

claims.text: Pattern-mining from workflow literature and vendor documentation to derive the pattern catalogue, followed by a systematic evaluation of major commercial workflow management systems of the early 2000s against every pattern, checking which each product actually supports.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- The pattern catalogue itself is a conceptual contribution, validated by whether practitioners found it a complete, non-overlapping vocabulary - which it largely has proven to be, cited thousands of times since.
- The vendor-support evaluation is a snapshot of early-2000s products and is now dated as a product comparison.
- The patterns themselves remain the standard reference and were later extended by the same research group (data patterns, resource patterns, exception-handling patterns) rather than superseded.
